text:
The physician may be found liable if they failed to screen this 78-year-old for vertebrobasilar insufficiency risk (for example, with a pre-treatment vertebral artery/provocative test) and did not obtain informed consent about the stroke risk. They then applied an articulatory springing technique with cervical rotation and extension. The post-treatment confusion, nausea, and vertigo point to vertebrobasilar ischemia or vertebral artery injury, so skipping that screening and consent would breach the standard of care.

CONFIDENCE: 70
